claims.text: Machine-learning models trained on alloys with known thermal-conductivity properties can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
A diverse high-entropy-alloy training dataset and validation against experimental data are conditions for applying the predictive approach.
Alloy microstructure and chemical composition are predictive mediators for phonon thermal conductivity.
The predictive approach can learn patterns in alloy data that correlate with low phonon thermal conductivity.
Specific atomic arrangements can correlate with low phonon thermal conductivity.
Lattice distortions can correlate with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The approach will accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The approach will outperform current thermal-conductivity predictions by at least 20%.
The approach is applicable only to high-entropy alloys whose compositions and microstructures are similar to those represented in the training dataset.
The approach may generalize poorly to alloys with substantially different compositions or microstructures.
Additional training data may improve the approach's predictive accuracy.
A mean absolute prediction error greater than 30% in experimental thermal-conductivity measurements would falsify the hypothesis.
